column1: # Pinned compile verdict for every .pd under stdlib/.
# This file is the machine-readable half of stdlib/STATUS.md. It is enforced by
# scripts/stdlib-gate.sh (`make stdlib-gate`), which recompiles every file and
# fails on any of:
#   REGRESSION       a file the language used to accept is now rejected
#   XPASS            a file recorded as rejected is now accepted (update this file)
#   VERDICT_CHANGED  still rejected, but at a different stage
#   BLOCKER_CHANGED  still rejected at the same stage, but for a different reason
#   file-set drift   a .pd was added to or removed from stdlib/
# Columns (tab-separated):  path  verdict  blocker
# VERDICT vocabulary:
#   COMPILE_OK        compiles and links (requires a `fn main`)
#   ACCEPTED_NO_MAIN  the language accepts the file; only `fn main` is absent.
#                     This is the verdict a *working* stdlib module would carry,
#                     since library modules have no main. Without it the XPASS
#                     check would be unreachable for every file here, and the
#                     gate would be unable to report the one thing it promises.
#   COMPILE_FAIL      rejected by the lexer, parser or type checker
#   LINK_FAIL         REFUSED, no longer declarable. It meant "accepted by the
#                     compiler, rejected by gcc", which is never a property of a
#                     FILE: if pdc accepted the source, C that will not build is a
#                     defect in pdc. scripts/stdlib-gate.sh now rejects a row that
#                     names it, and gate_probe no longer emits it — that outcome
#                     comes back as BACKEND_REJECT / BACKEND_UNRESOLVED, which fail
#                     the gate whatever this file declares. Zero rows used it.
# BLOCKER is the FIRST construct pdc rejects, which is a floor and not the full
# bill: lexing is a whole-file pass, so a lexer-level blocker anywhere in a file
# masks every parser-level blocker in it. stdlib/prelude.pd USED to be recorded
# as ATTRIBUTE because of `#[cfg]` on line 163; that lexical blocker is gone
# (N2-10), and the file is now recorded as USE_DECL — which is exactly the
# "18 `use` declarations the parser would reject next" this paragraph predicted.
# The prediction being borne out is the evidence that the floor was a floor.
# Blocker categories, each independently reproduced by a one-line probe (the
# probes are listed in stdlib/STATUS.md):
#   USE_DECL         `use path::to::Item;`      — no module system
#   MOD_DECL         `mod name;`                — no module system
#   PUB_FN_IN_IMPL   `pub fn` inside an `impl`  — visibility on methods
#   ASSOC_TYPE       `type Output;` in a trait  — no associated types
#   GENERIC_DEFAULT  `<Rhs = Self>`             — no generic parameter defaults
#   UNINIT_LET       `let mut v: T;`            — declaration without initialiser
#   RAW_POINTER      `*mut T`                   — no raw pointer type
#   SHIFT_ASSIGN     `x >>= 1;`                 — no compound shift assignment. `>>=`
#                    is not one token: the lexer produces `>` then `>=`, and the
#                    parser reports "Expected expression, but found '>='".
# RETIRED CATEGORIES, and the five rows they moved. All three were LEXICAL, and
# lexing is a whole-file pass, so each was masking every parser-level blocker in
# its file — which is what the header above says a blocker is a floor and not a
# bill. N2-08…N2-11 removed all three, and the rows below now record the blocker
# that was always behind them. Not one file moved closer to compiling: this is
# the same debt, measured one layer deeper.
#   ATTRIBUTE        `#[...]`                   — RETIRED at N2-10/N2-11. `#` lexes;
#                    an attribute is now refused by the PARSER, by name, and
#                    every one of these files hits a `use` or `*mut` first.
#   CHAR_ESCAPE      `'\t'`                     — RETIRED at N2-09. Escapes lex in
#                    char literals; stdlib/std/string.pd's next blocker is `use`.
#   FLOAT_LITERAL    `3.14`                     — RETIRED at N2-03. `3.14` is one
#                    token; stdlib/std/math.pd's next blocker was `^`.
#   BITWISE_XOR      `a ^ b`                    — RETIRED at N5-12. `^` is an
#                    operator now, and stdlib/std/math.pd's next blocker is the
#                    `pub const` on its first line: CONST_ITEM. Third time this
#                    file has moved a layer deeper without moving closer to
#                    compiling, which is what the header means by a blocker
#                    being a floor and not a bill.
#   CONST_ITEM       `pub const PI: f64 = …;`   — RETIRED at N3-09. Top-level
#                    `const` and `static` items parse, type-check and emit, so
#                    stdlib/std/math.pd's six `pub const` lines are no longer a
#                    blocker at all; its next one is `e >>= 1;` at line 50:
#                    SHIFT_ASSIGN. FOURTH move for this one file, and the first
#                    that was not lexical — which is the same lesson from the
#                    other side: a PARSER-level blocker also masks everything
#                    behind it, and the only thing measuring it establishes is
#                    where the floor is now.
